a: Emotional and social well-being, including how we cope and connect.
Only whether someone has a diagnosis.
Feeling happy all the time.
why: Mental health is part of everyday well-being. People experience it differently, and support can help.

q: Does struggling with mental health mean someone is weak?
a: Yes, they should try harder.
No. Anyone can struggle and deserves care.
Only if they ask for help.
why: Mental health difficulties are not a character flaw. Listen without blame or judgment.

q: You feel overwhelmed after a stressful day. What could help?
a: Ignore your needs and keep working.
Use alcohol to switch off.
Try a small break, a grounding exercise, or talking with someone you trust.
why: Small coping steps can ease stress. Different things help different people; these steps do not replace care when more support is needed.

q: When is it reasonable to seek professional support?
a: Only when things become unbearable.
When distress persists, affects daily life, or you want help understanding it.
Only after an online quiz gives a diagnosis.
why: You can ask a qualified health professional for support without waiting for a crisis. A learning quiz cannot diagnose you.

q: A friend says they are having a hard time. What is a helpful first response?
a: Listen and ask what kind of support they would like.
Tell them other people have it worse.
Promise to fix everything yourself.
why: You do not need perfect words. Taking someone seriously and asking what they need can make it easier to talk.

q: You want emotional support in Vietnam but do not know where to begin. What is an option?
a: Wait until you can explain everything perfectly.
Keep it to yourself because helplines are only for other people.
Choose a support service that fits your situation, or ask a trusted person to help you contact one.
why: For emotional distress, Ngày Mai or HOPE may help. For a child’s safety or emotional needs, contact the National Child Helpline (111). For gender-based violence, CSAGA offers support; Peace House supports women, young people and children affected by violence or trafficking. Phone numbers, opening hours and service details are below.

q: What if the support line is closed or you cannot get through?
a: It means you do not deserve support.
Try another source of support: a trusted person, a health professional, or a local health service.
Assume there are no other options.
why: One unavailable service does not mean help is unavailable. Check the opening hours and who each service supports, or contact a trusted person or health professional. If someone is in immediate danger, seek emergency medical help or go to the nearest emergency department; do not wait for a helpline to open.

q: What does finishing this quiz tell you?
a: You have a mental health diagnosis.
You should handle every difficulty alone.
You have explored some basics and ways to find support.
why: This is an educational activity, not a diagnosis or a test of your worth. You can revisit it or continue to the story parts.
